knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The SDS and label give the product's dilution, PPE and first aid. Other sources do not set the product's controls.
A mixture can create hazards that neither product has alone, so mixing is refused unless the label or SDS allows it.
Solvent-soaked rags carry fire and vapour risk. A closed metal container away from heat is the approved approach.

practicalCriteria: SDS and label checked, and controls identified, before any product is opened
Products not mixed, and any proposed mixture refused and recorded
Rags and residue stored and disposed of as the procedure sets out
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80% or higher. With three checks this means all three must be correct. Practical sign-off is separate: every practical criterion must be observed and met by the assessor. A knowledge pass is not practical competence and does not count toward sign-off.
evidenceRequired: Chemical register entry with SDS reference
stopWorkCriteria: Products mixed without label or SDS approval
Product used without its SDS controls
Solvent rags stored in an open or hot area
